correctness.rationale: At fixed q,u,v, unitary conjugation gives the lower-triangular kernel r^(j−i)√(d_j/d_i)/j, r=√q, a compact diagonal times a bounded geometrically summable operator. In odd/even blocks the even-to-odd transfer starts at lag one and the odd-to-even transfer at lag zero, giving F(z)=(1−qz)⁻¹[[1,ar z],[r/a,1]]. Discarding the first block and replacing the remaining paired diagonal by 1/(2k) changes the operator only by finite rank and a summable O(k⁻²) diagonal times a bounded operator. For the counting lemma in RESULT.md lines 47–59 I checked the limit without assuming uniform convergence of symbol counts at atoms: for a banded symbol, cut the block indices at finitely many fixed scaled points x=tk on [ε,R], chosen at continuity points of the symbol distribution. Separating the pieces costs rank bounded independently of t. The head costs at most dε/t+O(1) rank, and the tail has norm below t for R>||B_F||. On each middle piece, the smallest and largest diagonal values sandwich the weighted singular numbers by scaled unweighted singular numbers; block circulants differ by bounded rank and sample the symbol on a Fourier grid. Upper and lower sums converge to the integral of the symbol counting function as the scaled mesh shrinks and ε→0. Uniform approximation by band symbols then uses tN(ηt;D(B_F−B_M))≤d||B_F−B_M||/η and the singular counting inequalities at (1±η)t. Trace-class errors have tN(t)→0; count inversion applies since the coefficient is positive. With two indices per block the coefficient is (4π)⁻¹∫||F||_*; the determinant modulus is 1/Δ and the Frobenius norm squared is [2+q(a²+a⁻²)]/Δ². The two-by-two nuclear norm identity gives the displayed integral. Its strict increase in a²+a⁻² gives absolute log-contrast only, not parity. The neutral pair folds to the scalar symbol; equal Bloch singular values force equal column norms and zero inner product, i.e. a=1 and z=−1. At z=−1 the squared difference is q(a−a⁻¹)²/(1+q)². Compactness reduces the nonzero spectrum to eigenvalues, and the first nonzero coordinate plus the explicit polynomial-growth binomial eigenvectors give exactly 1/j. The Schatten and log-average consequences follow from s_n∼K/n. The supplied checker was inspected, not run; there is no required finite computational proof step.

originality.rationale: The leading indexed law is a direct specialization of the existing Birman–Solomyak classical matrix-valued pseudodifferential Weyl law (as stated in Ponge §2.3, and also obtained from his Theorem 4.1). The circle/positive-frequency realization meets the hypotheses and gives exactly the claimed contrast-dependent integral, not just a finite-section distribution or the scalar subcase. The strict recovery of absolute contrast and the band meeting/splitting follow by elementary two-by-two matrix identities for the same symbol; the spectral and summability consequences do not provide a distinct new remainder. This is positive prior-implication evidence, not a finding of an identical earlier printed weighted Cesàro formula or a rejection based on inaccessible literature.

value.rationale: The geometric alternating weights and contrast diagnostic are natural, and the elementary counting proof can be helpful exposition. As a research finding, however, the purported new invariant is determined mechanically by a prior indexed matrix-symbol theorem through the two-cell representation. Strict contrast sensitivity follows at once from the two-by-two trace norm, and the gap is the direct zone-edge eigenvalue calculation. There is no separate substantial result outside that coverage: no nonneutral remainder estimate, finite-index characterization, or recovery of the parity phase. Thus the record does not establish an independently valuable new exact fact under the stated standard.
